AbstractText.Label: PURPOSE
AbstractText.content: Hospitalization can be stressful for patients and their families. Pre-hospitalization information is crucial in establishing a good basis for patient satisfaction. In order to develop better preparatory material for parents, this qualitative study explored whether parents of children with cystic fibrosis, admitted to a UK Children's Hospital, felt adequately prepared for their child's admission.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN AND METHODS
AbstractText.content: Data were collected from twelve parents whose children had been admitted within the last two years for routine intravenous antibiotics. Semi-structured interviews were analyzed using thematic analysis.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Four themes emerged from the analysis: (1) preparing for admission, (2) the ward as a challenging environment, (3) changes in the parent-professional relationship and (4) the parental role in medical care.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Provision of adequate preparatory information is essential in reducing parental stress, influencing how future experiences are appraised and managed. Effective parent-professional communication and opportunities to participate in care are likely to improve parental satisfaction.

AbstractText.Label: PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS
AbstractText.content: Preparatory information prior to hospital admission greatly assists parents in making informed decisions and working as joint advocates in their child's inpatient care.
